subject.title: macOS update can leave manual-update loop and stale node host causing Gateway restart storm

question: For macOS managed updates that resolve to the already-installed version or leave repeated `ai.openclaw.manualupdate.*` launchd jobs, should OpenClaw short-circuit/refuse before service churn, dedupe and clean submitted jobs, or keep refreshing package/service state through the current restart path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes user-visible update semantics and launchd cleanup scope; automation should not choose that product/upgrade contract on its own.

options.title: Short-Circuit And Repair In Product
options.body: Treat proven same-version updates as no-op/refuse before stopping the service, add safe `manualupdate` stale-job cleanup and dedupe, and surface recovery through Doctor/Fix guidance.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Keep this issue open only as the manual updater-job tracker and move node skew plus UI/update.run policy to their existing canonical issues before implementation.

options.title: Keep Current Refresh Semantics
options.body: Continue refreshing package/service state even for same-version updates, but require stronger launchd handoff proof and stale-job detection before closing this report.

recommendation.title: Short-Circuit And Repair In Product
recommendation.body: Treat proven same-version updates as no-op/refuse before stopping the service, add safe `manualupdate` stale-job cleanup and dedupe, and surface recovery through Doctor/Fix guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored recent update/launchd recovery work and already provided maintainer-direction comments on related macOS update lifecycle trackers.
